name: Tiglath-pileser
overview: Tiglath-pileser was a male king of Assyria, as recorded in 2 Kings 15:29. The Bible identifies him primarily by his royal title, emphasizing his role as a significant Assyrian ruler during the period covered in the Old Testament. There are no additional tribal or personal notes provided about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Tiglath-pileser means 'my trust is in the son of [the temple] Esharra,' reflecting a connection to Assyrian religious heritage, though it was not a name given by God. He is also referred to by the title 'King of Assyria,' which straightforwardly identifies his political authority. An alternate spelling, Tilgath-pilneser, appears in 1 Chronicles 5:6 with the same meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Tiglath-pileser beyond his identification as king of Assyria. No specific relatives or tribal affiliations are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tiglath-pileser is significant in the biblical narrative as a major Assyrian monarch who played a role in the geopolitical events affecting Israel and Judah. His reign marks a period of Assyrian expansion and influence, which impacted the history and prophetic messages concerning God's people. While the Bible does not elaborate on his personal story, his presence as king of Assyria situates him as a key figure in the unfolding divine plan recorded in Scripture.
